plain: A bond records a promise to pay under specified terms. Start by identifying the issuer, the type of bond and whether an obligation remains outstanding. A printed amount is not the same as today’s value.
professional: Classify the debt instrument, identify the obligor and distinguish the stated denomination from outstanding principal, redemption entitlement and supported market or collectible value.
checks: Exact issuer name, country, instrument type and identifier, if present.
Issue date, maturity, coupon, amendments and cancellation markings.
Evidence of ownership and the institution that can confirm the position.
steps: Record the wording and photograph both sides.
Compare the instrument with the relevant issuer/reference records.
Ask the issuer, successor, transfer agent or custodian what remains payable and what evidence they require.
name: Bonds and financial certificates

plain: An SBLC is a bank undertaking to pay a beneficiary when a demand meets its terms. It is not a promise that any holder can turn its face amount into cash. Start with the business purpose and the banks involved.
professional: Review the undertaking’s issuer, applicant, beneficiary, operative terms, expiry, presentation requirements, applicable rules and amendments. Distinguish issuance/advising evidence from an uploaded purported SWIFT message.
checks: Issuing/advising bank, applicant, beneficiary and undertaking reference.
Amount, currency, expiry, drawing conditions and all amendments.
Authority to request information and an independently established institutional confirmation channel.
steps: If applying, explain the underlying obligation to your bank’s trade-finance team.
Ask the bank which application, credit, collateral and fee requirements apply to your case.
If holding a document, obtain authorized institutional confirmation before relying on it.
name: SBLCs and bank guarantees

plain: First identify the exact asset. Savings bonds, outstanding securities and collectible certificates follow different paths. Inheriting the paper does not by itself establish who can redeem or transfer the asset.
professional: Identify the security and registration, establish estate or beneficiary authority, and investigate the current issuer/successor and obligation status. Separate transferable or redeemable rights from scripophily value.
checks: Names and registration on the document, series, dates and serial/identifier.
Any named co-owner or beneficiary and evidence of estate authority.
Issuer/successor status and whether a redemption or transfer process applies.
steps: Keep originals safe; start with copies for preliminary research.
Use the issuer’s official deceased-owner or transfer instructions.
Ask an estate professional or the relevant institution which authority documents are needed.
name: Inherited bonds and documents

plain: Start with what the object or material is, where it is, who owns it and what independent testing supports the description. A photograph, stamped number or report cannot answer every question about the physical item.
professional: Document identification, quantity/weight, fineness or grade, assay or laboratory evidence, provenance, chain of custody, title and location. Distinguish report-record matching from physical authentication and valuation.
checks: Photographs, markings, measured quantity and current physical location.
Refiner, assay or gem laboratory report and its scope/date.
Ownership, custody and any transfer or shipment restrictions requiring specialist review.
steps: Identify the relevant specialist: assay/refinery for metals, gem laboratory for stones, qualified laboratory for mineral samples.
Check report details using the issuing organization’s official service when available.
Arrange an appropriate physical inspection before relying on a sale or valuation claim.
name: Gold, gemstones and minerals

plain: That is a valid starting point. Names such as “golden dragon,” “golden drum” or “golden gun” need context. We should not assume they identify a recognized financial instrument, a particular material or an item with redeemable value.
professional: Treat informal labels as unclassified claims. Establish the object/document, issuer or maker, provenance and relevant jurisdiction before assigning an instrument class or economic interpretation.
checks: Exact wording, language, photographs, markings and dimensions.
Who supplied the description and what evidence supports it.
Whether this is a document, a commodity, a collectible or another physical object.
steps: Describe only what you can observe, separately from what someone told you.
Open a private project to organize the evidence.
Choose the appropriate qualified specialist after initial classification; actual firearms require an appropriate specialist route.
name: Unfamiliar names and unidentified items

plain: “Trade desk” can mean very different things. A securities desk, a bank’s trade-finance department and a bullion desk handle different needs. Start with your asset and goal, then check the organization’s stated services and eligibility.
professional: Route by instrument, transaction objective, jurisdiction and counterparty mandate. Distinguish securities execution/distribution from documentary trade finance and physical commodity dealing; institutional acceptance remains case-specific.
checks: Does the organization publicly document the service you need?
Which customers, jurisdictions, instruments and minimum sizes does it accept?
Are the representative, mandate and official contact channel independently established?
steps: For SBLCs/guarantees, ask for the bank’s trade-finance or guarantees team.
For securities, identify an appropriate broker/dealer, transfer agent or custodian according to the objective.
For metals, choose a relevant bullion dealer/refiner and inspection/custody specialist.
name: Find the right desk or professional

plain: A token is a digital record. It needs a clear explanation of the rights it represents. Recording a claim on a blockchain does not make the underlying asset genuine, valuable or acceptable to a lender.
professional: Separate ledger observations, control evidence, legal title, underlying custody, token-holder rights, issuance permissions and transfer restrictions. Oracle outputs are source-dependent attestations, not independent asset authentication.
checks: Network, public wallet/contract address and claimed rights.
Underlying asset evidence and the custodian or responsible issuer.
Legal terms, permitted transfers and the exact scope/freshness of any attestation.
steps: Organize the underlying rights and evidence first.
Review public ledger observations and obtain suitable technical/legal review.
Consider issuance only after the required approvals and operating arrangements exist.
name: Wallets, contracts and tokenization
